name: Question 6
problem: A company produces replacement batteries for a particular cell phone model at three locations. Location $A$ produces $30%$ of the batteries, of which $3%$ are defective. Location $B$ produces $38%$ of the batteries, of which $5%$ are defective. And location $C$  produces $32%$ of the batteries, of which also $5%$ are defective. What is the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective?
worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that the battery is defective, and

- let $A$ be the event that the battery was produced at location $A,$

- let $B$  be the event that the battery was produced at location $B,$

- let $C$  be the event that the battery was produced at location $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since  location $A$ produces $30%$ of the batteries,  location $B$ produces $38%$ of the batteries, and location $C$ produces $32%$ of the batteries, we have

$$
P(A)=0.3,\,P(B)=0.38,\,P(C)=0.32.
$$

- Since $3%$ of the batteries produced at location $A$, $5%$ of the batteries produced at location $B$, and $5%$ of the batteries produced at  location $C,$ are defective, we have 

$$
P(D|A)=0.03,\,P(D|B)=0.05,\,P(D|C)=0.05.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C) \\  & =(0.03)(0.3)+(0.05)(0.38)+(0.05)(0.32) \\  & =0.009+0.019+0.016 \\  & =0.044.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

A company produces replacement batteries for a particular cell phone model at three locations. Location A produces 30% of the batteries, of which 3% are defective. Location B produces 38% of the batteries, of which 5% are defective. And location C produces 32% of the batteries, of which also 5% are defective. What is the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective?

a
0.541
b
0.058
c
0.056
d
0.054
e
0.044
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let D be the event that the battery is defective, and

  • let A be the event that the battery was produced at location A,

  • let B be the event that the battery was produced at location B,

  • let C be the event that the battery was produced at location C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

P(D)=P(D∩A)+P(D∩B)+P(D∩C)=P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since location A produces 30% of the batteries, location B produces 38% of the batteries, and location C produces 32% of the batteries, we have P(A)=0.3,P(B)=0.38,P(C)=0.32.

  • Since 3% of the batteries produced at location A, 5% of the batteries produced at location B, and 5% of the batteries produced at location C, are defective, we have P(D|A)=0.03,P(D|B)=0.05,P(D|C)=0.05.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective is

P(D)=P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)=(0.03)(0.3)+(0.05)(0.38)+(0.05)(0.32)=0.009+0.019+0.016=0.044.
